A weave that becomes a trace

Open strands, visible crossings, trace-like ends. The mark describes a relationship between projects, without turning Braids into a separate company. [2][3][13]

Helix

A compact evolution of the prototype. Lively, but the vertical twist can read as DNA and says little about a trace.

Confluence

Three inputs meet one line. Clear at small sizes, but a merge symbol suggests the projects or their data become one.

Open weave

Recommended

Three distinct strands cross, then finish as staggered spans. The gaps make the weave work in one colour as well as orange.

Use the 16–24px optical master for small icons: slightly heavier strokes, taller spacing and wider crossing gaps. Use the standard master from 32px upwards. Keep clear space of ¼ of the mark’s width on every side. Minimum size: 16px. No enclosing shield, gradients or rotation. Crossings are transparent masks, so the mark works on any surface.

Sentient carries the feature name in display lockups. Keep the parent’s Inter wordmark and original watchtower intact. In the app, use Inter for “Braids”, including headings and navigation. [1][2][11]

A name with a useful verb

Short, concrete and a little playful. Headline options below follow the website’s direct feature language; the supporting copy explains the mechanism. [3][4][10][14]

  1. One trace. Every project.
  2. Follow the call across projects
  3. Your agents work together. Now their traces do too.
  4. A shared trace for every agent involved
  5. Bring matching spans into one trace
  6. From specialist agent to orchestrator
  7. Several projects. One continuous trace.
  8. Braid your projects together

Product description

Braids brings spans from several projects into one trace in LangWatch. An organisation admin chooses a target project and an OpenTelemetry filter, so matching spans from a source project appear in the target project’s traces. The spans stay in their original project; nothing is copied. Calls can be cryptographically signed, and a braid can require verified calls so only genuine calls are shown. Available on Enterprise, Braids lets you follow the call from your orchestrator to its specialist agents across project boundaries.

Use the name naturally

Create a braid
Braid into Web orchestrator
Braided from Specialist agents

“Braids” for the feature. “A braid” for one configured connection. Keep “signed” for verified calls, never for the feature as a whole.

Recommended launch line: “One trace. Every project.” Pair it with “Braid matching spans into your orchestrator’s traces” so the matching condition stays clear.

Files to work with

The HTML embeds every font and drawing. SVG downloads are self-contained, with transparent marks and embedded fonts in text-bearing assets.

braids-mark.svgbraids-mark-dark.svgbraids-mark-app.svgbraids-mark-app-dark.svgbraids-mark-mono.svgbraids-mark-small.svgexploration-helix.svgexploration-confluence.svgbraids-lockup.svglangwatch-braids-lockup.svgbraids-empty-state.svgbraids-enterprise.svgbraids-docs-hero.svgbraids-og.svg

SVGs with text retain editable text and embed the source fonts. For print tools that ignore SVG web fonts, install the website’s Inter and Sentient fonts or outline text before export. Exploration files are not recommended production marks.

Grounded in the source

Implementation wins where older design notes differ. No website or product source files were changed.

[1] Website palette and typography

src/index.css

The implemented @theme and @font-face definitions. White paper, charcoal ink, website orange, three font roles, 14px cards and rounded buttons.

[2] Parent logo

src/components/Logo.tsx

The actual detailed watchtower path and Inter LangWatch wordmark. Reused without alteration in endorsed lockups.

[3] Feature branding

src/pages/LangyPage.tsx

A named feature inside LangWatch, with a small label, Sentient statement and a concrete product view. Braids follows that hierarchy.

[4] Launch composition

src/components/variants/VariantHero.tsx

Left-aligned display headline, quiet announcement pill, short capability-led body and dark primary action.

[5] Mesh and current colours

src/lib/mesh-colors.ts

Current warm #FFAF6E and cloud #CDDCF9. The kit uses a static field, with the text side protected.

[6] Mesh behaviour

src/components/MeshHeroBackground.tsx

White radial protection and a dissolved bottom edge. Static fallback used here so the weave is the only moving focus.

[7] Trace vocabulary and iconography

src/pages/ObservabilityPage.tsx

Lucide stroke icons, a dark trace window and staggered duration bars. This kit labels its diagram as project provenance, not span type.

[8] Product visuals

docs/design-system/patterns/feature-visuals.md

Precise, crisp product diagrams and stable colour meaning. Existing span-type colours must remain independent of project provenance.

[9] Motion

docs/design-system/tokens/motion.md

Still by default, 650ms ease-out, plays once and holds, explicit replay, reduced-motion support.

[10] Developer copy

docs/design-system/copy.md

Name the mechanism, use concrete product nouns, keep the supporting copy short.

[11] Product tokens

packages/design-system/src/system/config.ts

Inter for app headings and body, Sentient for display; orange semantic foreground/subtle pairs for badges.

[12] Product palette

packages/design-system/src/color-mode/color-system.ts

Product #ED8926, slate, orange foregrounds, plus purple. Brand identity stays orange; extra hues only identify projects.

[13] Starting prototype

dev/docs/plans/braids/braids-prototype.html

braidMark and hero: preserve over/under weaving and provenance, replace the vertical helix with an open horizontal trace form.

[14] Editorial constraints

CLAUDE.md

British English requested in the brief; the site also prohibits em dashes and real customer names.

Decided, 21 October 2026

The open weave is the mark and “One trace. Every project.” is the launch headline. The display wordmark is Sentient; Inter stays throughout the app. Website and product orange remain separate inherited tokens until the parent brand makes a wider palette decision.
